chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from al-Amriki ibn Ali, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a woman who gave birth from adultery, is it permissible for her milk to be used for suckling? He said, 'It is not permissible, nor is the milk of her daughter who was born from adultery.' And when the master of the girl who was impregnated by him is released from that [impediment], her milk becomes permissible.

key_terms.فُجِرَ بِهَا: She was impregnated / had illicit intercourse
key_terms.يُسْتَرْضَعَ: To be suckled / used for wet-nursing

ai.seo_question: Is the milk of a woman who gave birth from adultery permissible for suckling?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the milk of a woman or her daughter conceived through zina is initially impermissible for suckling due to the impediment of the father's status, but becomes permissible once the father is freed or the impediment is removed. This ruling highlights the nuanced Shia jurisprudence on how lineage and paternal status affect the validity of rida'ah (suckling) in establishing kinship and marriage prohibitions.
